instructions.task: Read each load or dispatch call in the line; the step is the heading of the numbered step it sits in, empty when it sits in none. Which part does a call leave out?

criteria.none: Every call says when to go (an IF condition, or a MUST at its point in the step), where (a named file, path or skill), what to do there, and what to bring back (a concrete result the step goes on to use). What to do there is said when the call names an action at the destination ('apply its test', 'run its check') or when the result names the work, as 'return the standards that apply' or 'return each case with its verdict' do; a separate 'to <work>' is needed only when the result alone doesn't show it.
criteria.when: A call gives no moment to go: no IF condition and no MUST, or a condition nobody could observe, such as 'if useful'.
criteria.where: A call names no destination the agent can open: no file, path or skill, or one too vague to find, such as 'the relevant reference'.
criteria.work: The result is too generic to show what to do at the destination, and the call names no action there, as in 'load the reference and return its findings' or 'consult the guide and report back'. A named result that implies the work is not this.
criteria.result: A call brings nothing back the step can use: no return, 'more context', 'the details', or a bare 'and return' with no result named.

when.finding: A call doesn't say when to go.

where.finding: A call doesn't say where to go.

work.finding: A call doesn't say what to do there.

result.finding: A call doesn't say what to bring back.

instructions.task: What does this section of a reference do?

criteria.stage: It owns a stage of work on its own: here the agent inspects something, judges it and decides, and this section is where that work is taught and finished. A section that has the agent run commands or read their output and then says what that output does and doesn't prove owns a stage, even when it lists the commands.
criteria.part: It is one part of a stage the reference as a whole owns, such as the stage's inputs, one of its signals, its examples or its stop, with the rest of the stage in other sections.
criteria.lookup: It is a lookup the agent consults rather than work it performs: a standards list, a table, a diagram, definitions, facts, or a list of shapes or templates. That includes a list of commands, queries or APIs with what each does or returns, a table mapping errors or symptoms to their fixes, a code pattern or helper to copy, a prompt or binding template, and a catalogue of rules or patterns to consult. Rules that govern a decision the agent makes in this section belong to that stage and are not a lookup.

instructions.task: Of what a stage's teaching needs (what to inspect, what good and bad look like, when to stop), which does the section leave out? The outline lists the reference's headings, and the opening holds the paragraphs under its title, where it says what it owns and what it returns. Teaching that the outline or opening shows the reference gives elsewhere counts for this section.

criteria.none: It says what to inspect, shows what good and bad look like, and says when the stage is done, in its own body or where the outline or opening shows the reference gives it, such as under a 'When to stop', 'Good and bad' or 'Examples' heading, or in a Return or Stop line of the opening. Good and bad can come through examples, signals, a contrast (a bad move named against the instruction, as 'quote the line; do not paraphrase it' is) or a standard the section names and judges against, such as the proof standards a reference loads; the section need not restate that standard. A stop can be the result the section or the reference returns.
criteria.inspect: It never says what to look at or open.
criteria.good_bad: It gives no picture of good and bad: no examples, signals, contrast or named standard to judge against, in its body or under another heading of the reference.
criteria.stop: It never says when the work of the stage is done, and neither the outline nor the opening shows a stop, a completion or a return the stage ends at.

inspect.finding: Section owns a stage but doesn't say what to inspect.

good_bad.finding: Section owns a stage but doesn't show what good and bad look like.

stop.finding: Section owns a stage but doesn't say when to stop.
